items.gist: The passage identifies beings associated with māyātattva and their progressive attainment of tattvas up to Ananta.
It describes Ananta's place, powers, and the Śiva-related hierarchy that governs creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
Māyābila and the guhā are presented as the womb of worlds, with countless rudras dwelling in its hidden chambers.
It distinguishes grades of nearness to the Lord and states that the many streams are too numerous to enumerate.
The avyaktakala, three folds, and granthi are explained as māyā's work, while māyātattva itself is formless and all-dissolving.
Ananta, lord of māyātattva, agitates atoms and produces countless coverings, while the śāstra enumerates related powers and authorities.
Beings with māyā-made bodies are absorbed and deluded by māyā, which misleads those lacking devotion and true knowledge.
Beyond mahāmāyā, the vidyātattva is described with its mantras, vidyeśvaras, and puras.
The aiśa tattva above vidyātattva contains the eight vidyeśvaras and their rulers.
The gurus summarize the descent from the guhā to the subtle rudras and the progressive establishment of beings.
The eight śaktis meditate on Ananta as the supreme cause, while the lower śiva-purity is marked as still to be transcended.
The passage names the kaṇcuka-like coverings and successive āvaraṇas from the aiśa level up to the purest covering.
